name: hcapp_logClientErrors
description: Stores a session-level client error log in HC.ClientErrorLog. No auth validation is performed — the @accessToken parameter is accepted for API consistency but intentionally not checked. Device registration is also not required: logs from de-registered devices are accepted so that failure patterns (e.g. repeated approveLogin token failures) can be captured for diagnosis. Each call inserts one row representing one session's accumulated exception log.

parameters.name: deviceId
parameters.description: Device UUID written directly to HC.ClientErrorLog.DeviceId. Does not need to exist in HC.Device — no FK constraint on that column. Passed as-is from the caller.

parameters.name: accessToken
parameters.description: Accepted for API consistency but intentionally not validated. The SP design requires that error logs from unauthenticated or de-registered devices are still accepted.

parameters.name: errorLog
parameters.description: Full session error log text. Exception entries are separated by newlines and '===' delimiters within the string. Written as-is to HC.ClientErrorLog.ErrorLog.

rowsets.name: Envelope
rowsets.description: Always present. On success: success=1, errorCode=NULL, errorType=NULL. On DB error: success=0, errorCode=1992, errorType=19. Standard success envelope.

columns.name: success
columns.description: 1 on success, 0 on unhandled DB error.

columns.name: errorCode
columns.description: Numeric error code. NULL on success. 1992 on DB error.

columns.name: errorType
columns.description: Error classification code. NULL on success. 19 on DB error.

rowsets.description: Returned only on unhandled DB error (CATCH block). Not present on success. Note: HC.ErrorLog INSERT uses userId=NULL since no auth was performed.

sideEffects: Inserts one row into HC.ClientErrorLog with DeviceId, ErrorLog, and LoggedAt (DEFAULT SYSDATETIMEOFFSET()).
Writes to HC.ErrorLog with userId=NULL on unhandled DB error.

codeSmells.detail: @errorLog is accepted and written as-is with no length or content validation. A NULL @errorLog would fail with a NOT NULL constraint violation on ClientErrorLog.ErrorLog, which would be caught by the CATCH block and logged as an unhandled error rather than a meaningful validation error.

@accessToken is accepted in the signature but is never read or used in the SP body. This is by design (documented in the SP header) but is a code smell per CLAUDE.md rules. The parameter cannot be removed without an API contract change.

breakingChanges: New SP — no HC5 predecessor. No breaking changes from migration.
Auth is intentionally skipped for this SP. Callers must not assume that @accessToken is validated.
